overview: This Senate resolution supports naming September "Dystonia Awareness Month." Dystonia is a neurological disorder that causes involuntary muscle contractions, leading to unusual movements and postures that can make walking, speaking or daily tasks difficult. The resolution estimates that 250,000 to 300,000 Americans have it, notes that it is often misdiagnosed and has no cure, and describes treatments such as injections, medications and deep brain stimulation. It also notes that service members and veterans can develop dystonia after brain injuries or other service-related conditions, and that the Defense Department has funded dystonia research. It calls for more research and encourages Americans to hold awareness activities. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say awareness can lead to earlier diagnosis of a frequently misunderstood condition and build support for research into better treatments.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding for dystonia research.
